measureRecords.whatItDoes: Let the existing temporary 0.3% city sales and use tax for a community recreation pool also pay for operating and maintaining the pool and related pool capital improvements. The tax rate would stay the same and its existing December 31, 2050 end date would remain. The city could keep revenue already collected and use it for these purposes. It could enter a financial agreement lasting beyond the current fiscal year to pay the pledged revenue, including earlier collections, to the Cañon City Area Metropolitan Recreation and Park District. These pledged receipts could be retained and spent outside legal revenue limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the expanded pool uses, use of previously collected revenue, multi-year payment agreement and proposed revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve these proposed changes to the existing pool tax through this question.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Extend the school property-tax levy approved in 2017 that is scheduled to expire, with no new end date. The district would set the rate needed to continue raising $1,385,000 a year for its general fund, in addition to other general-fund property taxes. Money would support all district schools, including Mountain View Core Knowledge School, for preschool opportunities, student technology, school safety, recruiting and keeping teachers and staff, and career training, internships, college credit and industry credentials.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Continue the expiring school levy on an ongoing basis for the stated education uses.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not extend this expiring levy through this measure.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Add a property-tax levy of no more than 6.9 mills to the district’s existing levy, authorizing $361,851 in 2026 for collection in 2027 and the amounts it generates in later years. Money would support the district’s capital and general-fund needs, including volunteer recruitment, availability of firefighters and emergency medical technicians, fire and emergency medical services, and phased replacement of aging emergency vehicles. Spending would remain subject to state laws, regulations and district accountability and transparency policies. Tax revenue and its investment earnings could be retained and spent under the proposed constitutional and other legal revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional district property-tax levy and the proposed revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional levy or its proposed revenue-limit exception.
